tasks.title: Sliding an arrow caption along its route
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. A user selects an arrow that carries a caption, presses on the caption with the selection tool and slides the pointer: the caption follows, but stays glued to the arrow's route (straight, bent or orthogonal), and the arrow remembers where along its route the caption sits so later reshaping keeps it there. Identify exactly 6 implementation functions by these semantic roles: (1) the selection-tool pointer-move hook that claims the gesture whenever it began on the caption, switches the cursor to a closed hand, and only starts moving anything once the pointer has travelled past a zoom-scaled distance or a move is already underway; (2) the editor-level step that turns the pointer, minus the grab offset recorded at press time, into a fraction along the route, writes that fraction plus re-centred coordinates onto the caption, and flags the editor as mid-gesture; (3) the routine returning the 0..1 share of total arc length nearest a scene location, choosing the nearest piece of the route and converting its local t value into accumulated length, or nothing for an empty or zero-length route; (4) the per-arrow memo that splits the route into pieces, measures each, builds running totals, and is invalidated by the shape's revision counter; (5) the decomposition that turns an arrow into ordered pieces, treating orthogonal arrows as sharp-cornered straight runs and otherwise returning either the bent pieces or the straight ones, never a mix; (6) the math-package search for the Bezier t value nearest a location: coarse sampling at evenly spaced values, then a shrinking-window refinement around the best sample. Explain how one pointer move flows through these, then answer: What keeps the caption from jumping so its centre sits under the cursor when grabbed? If the press lands where the caption overlaps the middle-segment knob, which wins? Is a sub-threshold move still claimed by the hook? For an orthogonal arrow with rounded corners, does the caption follow the rounded corners? Base your explanation on this checkout's implementation; do not modify code.

tasks.title: Stepping up caption type inside an oval
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. Identify exactly 6 implementation functions by these semantic roles: (1) the shared routine behind the bigger/smaller-type commands and the explicit picker that rewrites every selected piece of writing via a caller-supplied rule, re-lays each one out, keeps free-standing auto-width writing visually anchored per its alignment, afterwards refreshes connectors attached to the writing, and only remembers a new default when all results agree; (2) the relayout step that re-breaks the original unbroken source to the host's usable width, re-measures it, enlarges the host's height and/or width when the measurement no longer fits, and repositions the writing inside the host; (3) the inverse sizing formula giving the outer host extent required for an inner measurement, with different padding multipliers for ovals, rhombi, connectors and everything else; (4) the source-of-truth row breaker that returns visual rows with source offsets, falls back to hard breaks only when the available width is non-finite or negative, and keeps any already-fitting hard row untouched; (5) the fallback that splits a single over-long token glyph by glyph using cached per-glyph advances, leaving multi-codepoint emoji intact; (6) the finishing step for the final visual row of a hard row, which strips trailing whitespace only when the row overflows and then re-admits as many whitespace characters as still fit. Explain how one key press flows through these, then answer: When does the oval widen rather than only grow taller? Why is the alignment-anchoring step a no-op for the caption inside the oval? How are trailing spaces treated at an internal soft break versus at the end of a hard row? What is stored as the remembered default when several selected captions end with different values? Base your explanation on this checkout's implementation; do not modify code.

tasks.title: Turning a multi-selection with attached connectors
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. A user selects a captioned rectangle, an ellipse, an orthogonal connector between them, and a straight connector from the rectangle to an unselected diamond, then moves the turn knob while holding Shift. Everything swings around the selection's centre in set increments, the orthogonal connector is re-routed, and the straight connector lets go of the diamond. Identify exactly 6 implementation functions by these semantic roles: (1) the selection-tool pointer-move gatekeeper for transform knobs that defers to the cropping editor, refuses to turn selections containing frames or to transform a lone orthogonal connector, waits for a deliberate move when Alt is held on a scaling knob, snaps the pointer, and decides when proportional scaling is the default; (2) the group-turning routine that derives one shared angle from the pointer around the pivot, moves each member's centre around that pivot by the incremental amount while setting its absolute angle to original plus shared, and re-derives orthogonal connectors from their attachments instead of turning them; (3) the helper converting an orthogonal connector's two attachment locations into the connector's own relative coordinates so it can be re-routed; (4) the conversion from a stored proportional attachment ratio into a scene location on the target shape, honouring the shape's own angle; (5) the routine detaching one end of a connector, which removes the connector from the target's back-reference list only if the opposite end is not attached to the same target, and returns the former target's id; (6) the placement routine for a caption inside a host, honouring vertical and horizontal alignment, special-casing a sticky note's footer, and swinging the caption's centre around the host's content centre when the host is angled. Explain how one pointer move flows through these, then answer: Is the Shift increment applied by rounding or by flooring? What happens to the straight connector's two ends and to the diamond's back-references? Does the orthogonal connector's own angle change, and what is passed to it? What happens if a frame is part of the selection? Base your explanation on this checkout's implementation; do not modify code.

tasks.title: Deciding which overlapping shape a click picks
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. A user clicks where a turned, rounded-corner, unfilled rectangle lies over a filled ellipse; depending on whether the click lands on the stroke, near a rounded corner, or in the empty interior, the rectangle or the ellipse is picked. Identify exactly 8 implementation functions by these semantic roles: (1) the editor method that, given every candidate under the pointer ordered back to front, may prefer a selected one, else re-checks the front-most with half the usual tolerance and otherwise falls back to the one directly beneath; (2) the per-candidate editor predicate that short-circuits on a selected item's transform box, then accepts contact with the item's caption, before delegating to precise geometry; (3) the tolerance rule: the larger of half the stroke width plus a hair and a zoom-scaled base reach times a fudge factor; (4) the precise geometric check with a single-entry memo whose reuse depends on whether the remembered answer was positive or negative relative to the new tolerance, a cheap turned-box rejection, and a choice between interior-plus-outline and outline-only; (5) the policy deciding whether an interior counts: never for arrows, only closed loops for lines and freehand strokes, else when non-transparently filled, captioned, embedded content, writing or a picture; (6) the containment check casting a segment from the location away from the box centre and using the parity of distinct outline crossings, with a fill-polygon path for closed freehand strokes; (7) the how-far-from-the-outline calculation for box-like shapes that un-turns the location around the centre and takes the minimum over edges and corner arcs; (8) the cached decomposition of a box-like shape into four inset edges and four cubic corner arcs, substituting a tiny radius for sharp corners. Explain the flow, then answer: Which shape is picked for a click in the rectangle's empty interior, and why? If the rectangle is already selected, what does (1) return for that click, and which option changes it? Why are crossings de-duplicated? How does the memo avoid returning a stale miss when tolerance grows? Base your explanation on this checkout's implementation; do not modify code.

tasks.title: Attaching a moved arrow end among nested shapes

tasks.title: Eraser sweep marking, restoring and committing removals
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. tasks.title: Freeform loop selection with clusters and artboards

tasks.title: Alt-drag cloning of a moving selection
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. Identify exactly 8 implementation functions by these semantic roles: (1) the editor helper, invoked at most once per drag, that clones the moving set, resets the originals to their press-time positions, swaps the press bookkeeping (hit target, hit list, drag origin) over to the copies, and replaces the scene synchronously; (2) the per-object cloning step that gives a copy a fresh identity and timestamps, optionally a new roughness seed, and remaps cluster ids through a shared old-to-new table; (3) the recursive structural cloner that handles plain objects and arrays but skips the top-level memoised drawing artefacts; (4) the tiny revision helper that increments the counter, rolls a new random tiebreaker and stamps the time without notifying anyone; (5) the reordering pass, run before cloning, that makes the members of every cluster contiguous level by level from the outermost cluster inward, keeping first-appearance order and bailing out if anything would be lost; (6) the post-cloning fixer in the attachment module that rewrites label, host and arrow-endpoint references to point at copies, drops references whose target was not cloned, and re-routes right-angle connectors; (7) the fixer that points each copy's artboard membership at the clone of its original's artboard, or at none; (8) the editor method that, only when snapping applies, recomputes the stored spacing between neighbouring shapes used for equal-distance guides. tasks.title: Enacting an undo entry: repair, stacking and visibility
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout. A user presses undo after removing a shape that had arrows attached and an empty label. tasks.title: Ctrl+G clustering across artboards and nested edits

tasks.title: Picture bytes travelling between peers in a live room

If a payload id already exists in Bob's editor, what happens, and why can a vector picture's revision change on arrival? Base your explanation on this checkout's implementation; do not modify code.

tasks.title: Offline drawing persistence and cross-tab refresh
tasks.prompt: Investigate this Excalidraw checkout.
